items.title: Supernus and Indivior merge to create CNS mega-company with 11 approved drugs
items.snippet: Supernus Pharmaceuticals and Indivior Pharmaceuticals are outlining a combined expected $2.2 billion in annual revenue, plus $125 million in cost savings that will include “natural redundancies.”

items.title: BioNTech picks Sobi CEO Oelkers to lead as founders plot new mRNA biotech
items.snippet: BioNTech’s leadership transition was announced earlier this year, with CEO Ugur Sahin and CMO Özlem Türeci leaving to start a new mRNA company. Guido Oelkers of Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB will take over as CEO in early 2027.

items.title: Novo’s late-stage IL-6 stumble shakes inflammation space
items.snippet: Novo Nordisk was banking on the inflammatory benefits of its investigational therapy ziltivekimab to improve cardiovascular outcomes. Last week’s Phase 3 failure dashed not just the Danish pharma’s hopes but that of other drugmakers working on the same pathway.

items.title: ‘Unlikely’ AstraZeneca-BMS mega-merger would be largest pharma deal ever
items.snippet: If AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb were to successfully become one company, analysts say it could reset the current deal environment, which has picked up greatly in the first half of the year.

items.title: Amgen hit with cybersecurity breach, patient data affected
items.snippet: The hack is unlikely to affect Amgen’s financial reporting and other operations, nor does the pharma expect its ability to meet patient needs will be compromised.

items.title: Biologics push CMOs/CDMOs to expand sterile fill-finish and prefilled syringe capacity
items.snippet: As biologics, biosimilars and GLP-1s drive demand for sterile drug products, CMOs and CDMOs are investing in fill-finish, lyophilization, inspection and packaging capacity to keep pace with a dynamic injectable market.

items.title: Biotech leaders call for streamlining of INDs as FDA’s Trialblazer rolls out
items.snippet: The FDA’s new investigational new drug pilot program—one part of HHS’s broader clinical trial modernization initiatives—has lofty goals to expedite first-in-human trials of novel drugs, but experts say it won’t tip the scales much on its own.

items.title: 5 companies advancing ATTR assets in the wake of Wainua’s fail
items.snippet: The Phase 3 failure of AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ antisense therapy in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy last month left the space reeling—and readjusting. BioSpace looks at five contenders and where they currently stand.

items.title: Capricor CEO won’t rule out legal action against FDA after negative adcomm
items.snippet: After an FDA advisory committee voted 9-3 on Wednesday against recommending Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy drug for approval, stakeholders allege an “ulterior motive” and “biased intentions.”

items.title: Lilly and Resilience invest $750M in diabetes and obesity drug device supply
items.snippet: The investment will expand Resilience’s U.S. capacity to make the KwikPen device Eli Lilly uses to deliver its injectable diabetes and obesity medicines.

items.title: AbbVie shares pressured as Q2 I&I beat falls below investor expectations
items.snippet: AbbVie investors’ sky-high expectations led to a 4% share decline on Friday as the company reported more modest consensus beats than expected.

items.title: Novo's IL-6 inhibitor fails in cardiovascular Phase 3, plunging shares more than 9%
items.snippet: Novo Nordisk's IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab failed to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in the late-stage trial, dashing hopes for an edge in the hyper-competitive cardiometabolic space.

items.title: Moderna maintains 10% growth target despite Phase 3 norovirus miss
items.snippet: Moderna’s norovirus vaccine failed in a Phase 3 trial, but the company still has faith in an ambitious revenue growth target thanks to ex-U.S. vaccine sales and a unanimous FDA adcomm win for mFLUSIVA.

items.title: Alnylam absorbs $10.8B blowback after cutting full-year guidance for TTR franchise
items.snippet: Alnylam’s revenue cut “may create a near term credibility overhang and could “raise questions on peak sales potential, even if there’s tailwinds in the competitive landscape,” according to Stifel.

items.title: UniQure welcomes possible adcomm for Huntington’s asset as regulatory ‘jitters’ spread through biopharma
items.snippet: UniQure is ready to put its Huntington’s disease gene therapy through an advisory committee meeting—even as the broader rare disease space has been put on edge by recent FDA scrutiny of assets by Replimune and Capricor.

items.title: Replimune overcomes ‘messy data’ to secure positive adcomm vote for melanoma therapy
items.snippet: The FDA’s Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies advisory committee voted 10 to 3 in favor of Replimune’s immunotherapy for advanced melanoma in combination with Bristol Myers Squibb’s Opdivo, but trial design was a major sticking point as the panel deliberated.

items.title: BMS’ ‘big beat’ clouded by Cobenfy, heart disease data delays
items.snippet: Strong quarterly results are prompting Bristol Myers Squibb to lift its 2026 outlook, though the company is facing another delay for key Cobenfy Alzheimer’s data and a pushed-back readout for milvexian.

items.title: Regeneron’s ‘aversion’ to M&A questioned as bumper Q2 builds war chest
items.snippet: Calls for Regeneron to step up dealmaking have intensified as the company has established an $18 billion cash pile and suffered clinical trial setbacks.

items.title: Daiichi’s pipeline falls behind rivals as cash flow nears peak: analysts
items.snippet: With Enhertu and Datroway hitting their peak revenue and rivals flowing into the antibody-drug conjugate space, Jefferies cuts expectations for Daiichi Sankyo.

items.title: J&J secures right to take the helm in up to $925M Sail CAR T pact
items.snippet: As part of the collaboration, Johnson & Johnson will have an exclusive option to acquire Sail Biomedicines for an additional $2.58 billion.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

items.title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
items.snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?

items.title: Lilly just bought renowned regulator Peter Marks a pipeline to play with
items.snippet: FDA veteran Peter Marks will now shape the future of Eli Lilly’s vaccines work after the buys of Curevo, LimmaTech Biologics and Vaccine Company for up to $3.8 billion total.
